task: R291-B2 execution-level A/B (narrowed re-dispatch: only the judge and the readings were missing). One row, skill mcp-builder: run the commands literally written in the before/after SKILL.md; caliber copied from 06-benchmark/r285_exec_commands_ab.json.

caliber_note.commands_found: count of distinct literal command strings the extractor finds in THAT arm's SKILL.md text (triggers: python/python3/py, bash scripts/*.sh, npm test, pytest, cargo test, pip install, npx, open [), after removing inline-code backticks and dropping query-only forms (--help / --version / whoami / login). Denominator of every ratio in this file.
caliber_note.runnable: of those commands, how many were actually executed on this machine. A command whose toolchain is absent (cargo) is counted in commands_found and in blocked_not_runnable, and NEVER in runnable, rc_zero or artifacts.
caliber_note.rc_zero: numerator = number of runnable commands whose operative exit code was 0 in their normal (expected-to-pass) state. Expected-failure probes (state=RED, the doc's own Verify RED step) are excluded from the numerator and are reported separately as evidence for doc_claim_met. In this row one never-exiting service row (the inspector) is excluded
caliber_note.operative_rc: argv_resolved when cmdspec declared one (bare pytest is not on PATH in the managed venv), else argv_literal. Both argv lists are in detail_rows.
caliber_note.placeholder_unresolved: commands whose placeholders could not be resolved to a real input. All were resolved in this run (fixture .pptx and deck.html were built for it), so this is 0 everywhere; nothing is silently counted as failure.
caliber_note.persisted_artifacts: files newly appearing in that arm's OWN declared output directories, which are wiped before the arm runs and never shared between arms (the r283 contamination lesson). Paths are relative to the arm directory.
caliber_note.needs_external_account: commands that reach a third-party account gate before producing anything. Counted in commands_found, excluded from runnable / rc_zero / artifacts, and never counted as a doc defect: this run creates no external credential.
caliber_note.variant_rows: rows with primary === false are extra runs of the SAME doc literal with a different placeholder resolution (export-pdf with an absolute output path). They are evidence for the sub-claims and are NOT counted in commands_found, runnable, rc_zero or artifacts.
caliber_note.doc_claim_met: binary. mcp-builder A: the 3.2 Build and Test Python verify (python -m py_compile your_server.py) must return rc=0 and persist the compiled artifact. mcp-builder B: everything A claims PLUS the B-only codemod literal (npx @modelcontextprotocol/codemod@latest v1-to-v2) must run rc=0 and actually rewrite a v1-shaped project to v2 (source gained @modelcontextprotocol/server, lost the v1 sdk server import, manifest swapped).
caliber_note.unverified_rule: any arm whose commands could not be executed at all is reported UNVERIFIED with the command and its stderr and is excluded from both sides of every delta.
caliber_note.not_measured: executability and persistence only. This row does not measure the business quality of a generated MCP server, does not judge whether the codemod output is idiomatic, and does not re-run the r285 trio.
caliber_note.r289_command_fix: FIX(r289): the recorded judge command used `node -B`; -B is a python flag and this host rejects it (node rc=9 bad option). Judge command corrected to plain `node` and re-run: exit 0, same last line.
caliber_note.doc_claim_met_r285_original: binary. test-driven-development: the doc worked example must fail before the feature exists (RED rc!=0) and pass after (GREEN rc=0). frontend-slides: extracted-slides.json written by the doc-literal extract command must contain >=2 slides; the PDF half is reported separately as sub-claims (relative form vs absolute form) because the two differ. ui-ux-pro-max (cited): >=1 doc-literal command returning rc=0 that persists a design-system artifact.
caliber_note.blocked_not_runnable: commands_found items the machine could not execute (missing toolchain / ENOENT / declared runnable=false). Never in runnable, rc_zero or artifacts, and never counted as a doc defect.
caliber_note.service_rows_never_exit: NEW in this row (r285 had no such shape): npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector is an interactive UI that by design never returns, so its operative rc is a timeout signal (SIGNAL:SIGTERM) on both arms. It counts in commands_found and runnable, is excluded from rc_zero by the cmdspec (requires_rc_zero=false), and its evidence is the start-up banner predicate. That is what keeps this row from inflating the gain.
caliber_note.port_isolation: NEW: the surviving harness did not free the inspector ports between arms, so arm A SIGTERM-leftover server made arm B read rc=1 with MCP Inspector PORT IS IN USE at http://127.0.0.1:6274 - the r283 contamination one layer down (process, not directory). The relocated harness kills only leftover node/python pids holding 6274-6278 before each arm and records every kill in port_cleanup.

field_caliber_local.blocked_not_runnable: 0: npx and the managed python are both on the harness PATH, so nothing was missing-toolchain; no toolchain gap is disguised as a doc defect.
field_caliber_local.needs_external_account: 0: none of the three rows reaches a third-party account gate; this run creates no credential and does not record a 0 gain for it.
field_caliber_local.placeholder_unresolved: 0: your_server.py resolved by a fixture written before the row runs; the codemod dot operand by a v1-shaped fixture project => a fixture is never a produced artifact.
field_caliber_local.persisted_artifacts: one per arm: py_compile persists __pycache__/your_server.cpython-313.pyc in that arm s own py_work. The codemod edits in place and adds no file, so its effect is evidenced by the rewrite predicate plus the manifest swap, never by artifact counting.
field_caliber_local.executions: A=2 B=3 primary rows; no variant rows in this run (variant_executions=0).
